Messages.Author: avgrund
Messages.Body:
Good day fellow cold corpses.

Cards requiring a certain discipline/clan/sect must be played by a minion/vampire which have/fulfill these; but can these cards be stolen or acquired by minions not fulfilling the same?

For example a clan specific weapon on a vampire which is diablerized by another. Or a laibon retainer already on a vampire which changes sects.

Any special circumstance where this would be feasible (or not)?

Thanks for your help!

Messages.Author: Kraus
Messages.Body:
Hello!

Some clan specific cards have the requirement only in the initial equip action/occasion. They are free to be used by others however. For example, Blade of Bellona can be used by anyone but has to be equipped initially by a  .

Some cards specify that a certain requirement be met to be able to use it. Sword of Judgement is an example for these kinds of equipment.

> [LK:4]
> Cardtype: Equipment
> Clan: Salubri antitribu
> Melee weapon.
> Strike: strength +1 damage, with 1 optional maneuver each combat, only usable to maneuver to close range.
> Artist: Ginés Quiñonero

> Clan: Brujah antitribu

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> avgrund wrote:
> Cards requiring a certain discipline/clan/sect must be played by a minion/vampire which have/fulfill these; but can these cards be stolen or acquired by minions not fulfilling the same?
>
In general terms, yes - requirements are only important for playing the card. A Raven Spy requires Animalism, but once it's in play, you could move it to another vampire without any Animalism using Heidelberg Castle.

You might have a card, however, like Sword of Judgment which also includes the text: "Only usable by Brujah antitribu." And while a minion who is not a Brujah antitribu could have it, they couldn't use it.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
Some cards also use the following pattern:
"Requires a Sabbat vampire.
This Sabbat vampire can..."

If the card is moved to another vampire who is not Sabbat, that vampire cannot use the card.

There is a third way restrictions in use can be written such as Bowl of Convergence:

"If the bearer is a vampire who has Auspex [aus], the bearer gets +1 intercept. ..." which is the same as "The bearer with Auspex [aus] gets +1 intercept."
